title: WhatToLookAt: learned relations become a sensing budget
summary: WhatToLookAt takes the history-written relation machinery from SighImageFactorization and asks a compressed-sensing-style engineering question: if experience has already learned useful structure, how many future physical observations can be omitted? Gates 0–4 turn learned relations into an adaptive sensing budget. Gate 5 measures the price of sparse measurement rows. Gate 6 shows that sparse support geometry should be designed before observation. Gate 7 shows coverage alone is insufficient under signed multi-coordinate change. Gate 8 then deliberately buys measurement diversity with regular sparse overlap and reaches the robust 12-row frontier with a 9-row degree-3 code.

nodes.claim: Learns persistent relations from past temporal structure and uses them as a prior for future sparse sensing; local relation uncertainty withdraws sharing authority and purchases extra measurements only where confidence is low.
nodes.survived: Learned relations can replace future observations in controlled worlds; charged image-derived confidence and current residuals localize when extra sensing is needed; moderate measurement sparsity can reduce fan-in work; support geometry matters; coverage alone is insufficient; and Gate 8 shows that deliberately overlapping sparse measurements can recover robust multi-coordinate sensing with fewer interactions than generic 12-row sparse controls.
nodes.killed: Blind trust, shuffled confidence, coordinate memory and equal-cost random extra reads fail matched controls. Extreme row sparsity is not free. Post-hoc pruning is not equivalent to sparse-first design in the one-coordinate regime. Touching every coordinate once is insufficient. Gate 8 also kills the simplest degree-2-overlap hypothesis in this world: two measurement memberships per coordinate reach only 87.5% worst validation success, while degree 3 is the first structured design to clear the 95% target.

edges.why: WhatToLookAt explicitly states that it pushes the compressed-sensing question into the SighImageFactorization/Sihti lineage and operationalizes SighImageFactorization's learned relation state as a prior that can reduce future sensing.

WhatToLookAt explicitly names Sihti in its lineage and carries forward the operator-dependent-structure framing, but does not claim Sihti code inheritance; the new currency is measurement cost rather than residue location.
